sources.note: Nothing. Calls it 'a poorly-attested Munda language, apparently related to or a dialect of Asuri' and states, citing Census 2011 ST-15, that all Majhwars now record Indo-Aryan mother tongues (Chhattisgarhi, Surgujia, Sadri). Cites only Glottolog and the Census.

sources.citation: Office of the Registrar General, India. 2011 Census, Table ST-15: Scheduled Tribe by mother tongue (for each tribe separately) — Chhattisgarh / Uttar Pradesh, tribe 'Majhwar'.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); the open copy could not be downloaded when a reader tried
sources.note: Documents (per Wikipedia's citation) that the Majhwar tribe now reports only Chhattisgarhi/Surgujia/Sadri as mother tongue, i.e. no living Munda 'Majhwar' variety to describe; supports closing this key as undescribable rather than under-searched.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid page majh1236 'Majhwar' and reference record 304344 (Grierson 1906, hh bibliography).
sources.note: Nothing; bibliographic only. The reference record's language code field reads 'Manjhi = Majhwar [mmj]', confirming that the LSI 'So-called Mañjhi' of Raigarh (pp. 145-146) is the sole source behind Glottolog's Majhwar. Glottolog lists no other descriptive reference (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology).

sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. (ed.) 1906. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IV: Munda and Dravidian Languages. Calcutta: Office of the Superintendent of Government Printing. Section 'So-called Mañjhi dialect (State Raigarh)', pp. 145-146 (within Kherwari > Asuri, pp. 135-146).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library, call number 3254.1 F; Linguistics Library, call number CoPh 5.40; a Harvard library, call number Ud 0010
sources.note: Nothing. The Mañjhi section is a classification note (a form of speech 'between Asuri and Korwa', 'practically extinct', 'extremely corrupt and mixed with Aryan forms and words') plus the opening lines of the Prodigal Son; no Pronunciation or Accent paragraph; the author writes 'It would be waste of time and paper to go further into detail.' a full-text search for stress/accent the whole volume: accent statements exist only for Santali (p. 29), Mundari (p. 85, 'same as in Santali') and a Dravidian language (line 27204), none for Mañjhi/Asuri/Korwa.

sources.citation: Devy, G. N. (chief ed.), Chhattisgarh volume of the People's Linguistic Survey of India (Orient BlackSwan, Hindi/English), tribal-language entries for Sarguja/Raigarh (possible 'Majhwari'/'Manjhi' entry).
